impact.attacker_capability: Cause an administrative browser to execute attacker-controlled script on a selected sbx-* origin and compose that primitive with frame/origin and blob-URL disclosure steps.
impact.security_effect: Disclosure of the administrator-created flag.txt content through same-origin access to its rendered blob URL.

causal_trace.summary: An attacker controls the sandbox-token array supplied with rendered HTML to the shim through postMessage.

The authorization loop reuses the global, case-insensitive /allow-same-origin/ig RegExp. Its first successful test advances lastIndex, so a second identical forbidden token is not matched and is added to the iframe sandbox.
A duplicate allow-same-origin token combined with allow-scripts gives attacker-rendered content script execution under an sbx-* origin instead of the intended unique sandbox origin.
The official chain uses the resulting same-origin shim execution to obtain the randomized flag-rendering shim origin, read the nested iframe blob URL, and fetch the flag text.

failure.operation: iframe.sandbox.add(value) after a bypassed stateful forbidden-token test

primary_invariant.statement: Untrusted rendered content must not be granted the allow-same-origin iframe sandbox token; each requested token must be independently rejected or accepted before sandbox mutation.
primary_invariant.violated_because: The stateful global RegExp retains lastIndex after its first successful match, making the repeated authorization test depend on prior attacker-supplied array elements.

quality.review_notes: Organizer writeup and self-contained official exploit explicitly describe the global-RegExp lastIndex bypass and flag-fetch chain. The bundled direct shim artifact is not inspectable beyond its title, so exact shim source-line attribution is grounded in the organizer's quoted code rather than the shim artifact. No corrective patch, regression test, or recorded successful exploit execution is supplied. Later CSP, navigation, ancestorOrigins, and blob composition steps are browser/deployment-sensitive.

remediation.invariant_restored: Every requested sandbox token is evaluated with a non-stateful canonical membership check, and allow-same-origin is rejected before any iframe sandbox token is added.
mitigation_classes: deny allow-same-origin for untrusted rendered content

state_context.attacker_state_setup: Supply two consecutive allow-same-origin values followed by allow-scripts in the shim postMessage payload.
data_structure_invariants: The sandbox-token array must not result in allow-same-origin for untrusted content.
Authorization of each requested token must not depend on prior token checks.
state_context.state_machine: The global RegExp transitions from initial lastIndex to an advanced lastIndex after a successful first allow-same-origin match; the next test of the same token can fail, permitting sandbox mutation.

target.component: sandbox shim iframe renderer and its sandbox-token authorization
